s2523: In what order should the vehicles drive through the intersection when moving in the direction of the arrows, if the emergency service vehicle does not have its flashing blue special light switched on?
s2524: According to paragraph 1 of Article 51 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, the driver of an emergency or special service vehicle who has the flashing blue special light switched on and is carrying out an official task may depart from the requirements of Articles 25, 31–41 and 44 of this Law and of Annexes No. 1 and No. 2 of this Law, provided that road safety is ensured. A flashing red light may also be switched on in addition to the flashing blue special light. To obtain priority over other road users, the driver of such a vehicle must switch on the flashing blue special light and the siren. According to subparagraphs "a", "b" and "c" of paragraph 4 of Article 36 of the same Law, at an uncontrolled intersection: a) at an intersection of roads of unequal importance, the driver of a vehicle on the secondary road must give way to vehicles approaching on the main road, regardless of the direction in which they will continue; b) if the main road changes direction at the intersection, drivers on that road must follow the rules for intersections of roads of equal importance among themselves; drivers on the secondary road must also follow these rules among themselves; c) at an intersection of roads of equal importance, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right. Drivers of rail vehicles must follow the same rule among themselves. At such an intersection a rail vehicle has priority over a trackless vehicle, regardless of its direction of travel.

s2549: According to subparagraphs "a" and "c" of paragraph 4 of Article 36 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic, at an uncontrolled intersection: a) at an intersection of roads of unequal importance, the driver of a vehicle on the secondary road must give way to vehicles approaching on the main road, regardless of the direction in which they will continue; c) at an intersection of roads of equal importance, the driver of a trackless vehicle must give way to vehicles approaching from the right. Drivers of rail vehicles must follow the same rule among themselves. According to paragraph 4 of Article 51 of the same Law, a driver who has a flashing orange or yellow special light switched on and is carrying out construction, repair or cleaning work on the road, or is transporting valuables or securities in a cash-in-transit vehicle, or is carrying dangerous goods, or is driving an oversized or overweight vehicle, may depart from the requirements of road signs and markings and of paragraphs 5–10, 15 and 16 of Article 31 and paragraph 1 of Article 38 of this Law, provided that road safety is ensured. A flashing orange or yellow special light does not give priority over other road users; it is used to attract attention in order to prevent a possible danger.

s2581: According to subparagraph "b" of paragraph 7 and paragraph 8 of Article 32 of the Law of Georgia on Road Traffic: 7. Before turning right or left to enter another road or adjacent territory, without breaching the requirements of paragraph 2 of Article 20 of this Law and paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article, if the driver intends to leave the road: b) on the left, the vehicle must, as far as possible, move close to the centre line of the carriageway (on a two-way road) or to the left edge of the carriageway (on a one-way road), and if the driver intends to enter another two-way road, the turn must be made so that, on leaving the intersection of carriageways, the vehicle does not end up on the side for oncoming traffic. 8. If, because of the vehicle's dimensions or for another reason, the driver cannot make the turn in compliance with the requirements of paragraph 7 of this Article, departing from these rules is permitted, provided that traffic safety is ensured and other road users are not obstructed.
